newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 6.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on January 6. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Ismail Hasan Metareum, head of the minority Moslem-orientated United Development Party (PPP), said Indonesian society was already emotional and would easily explode if there were any corrupt practices or abuses of authority during this year's election.
Military authorities in Kalimantan said the situation in Sangau Ledo, where riots killed five people last week, has returned to normal.
Analysts expect President Suharto to unveil an austere budget for 1997/1998 when he addresses the national parliament on Monday.
Security forces say they know the identity of the person behind rioting last month in the town of Tasikmalaya in West Java and are hunting the local man who is their prime suspect.

Interior Minister Yogie Memet said political parties should work within the boundaries of new campaigning rules which restrict their activities in public rather than make an issue of the new regulations.
